mainEvent.title: Thu 11/19 · Anthropic's Nasdaq debut and Walmart, after hawkish Fed minutes
mainEvent.body: Anthropic priced its IPO at **$83** a share Wednesday evening, above the $70–78 range, and increased the offering size, Bloomberg reported citing a person familiar (via Reuters, Yahoo Finance); the company had not announced the price itself as of this evening. Shares are expected to start trading Thursday on Nasdaq as **ANT**. The October Fed minutes showed **almost all** officials see further hikes as likely appropriate and a couple open to more than 25bp in December, after Governor Waller called for a half-point hike. Thursday also brings **Walmart at 7:00a**, jobless claims and the Philly Fed at 8:30a, Fed's Goolsbee at 12:30p, and Intuit, Ross, Keysight and Gap after the close.

stories.title: Fed minutes: almost all officials see more hikes; Waller wants 50bp.
stories.body: Minutes of the Oct 27–28 meeting, where the Fed held at 3.75–4.00% in a 10–2 vote (Cook and Hammack wanted a 25bp hike), showed **almost all** participants judged further increases likely appropriate, up from "most" in September, and **a couple** said a move of more than 25bp could warrant consideration in December if inflation data were unfavorable. No one discussed a cut; many called the AI buildout a material source of inflation risk, and most flagged fast-growing, opaque AI-related debt (TheStreet, investingLive, The Private Banker). Earlier Governor Waller told CNBC a half-point hike is probably needed in December ("You might need to, like, shock people"), or the Fed must clearly signal another 25bp in January. CME FedWatch put about 10% on a 50bp December move Wednesday morning (TheStreet), and 69% on 50bp of hikes by the end of January (Yahoo Finance). The 10Y still slipped 4bp to 5.07%. Data are softening: pending home sales fell 4.7% in October vs about −2% expected, to a record low (Trading Economics, Yahoo Finance), and permits fell 7.4% even as starts jumped. The next decision is Dec 9; Kalshi has a 25bp hike at 91% and more than 25bp at 7%.

stories.title: Anthropic prices above range at $83; trading starts Thursday.
stories.body: Anthropic priced its IPO at **$83** a share, $5 above the top of its $70–78 range, and increased the offering size, Bloomberg reported Wednesday afternoon citing a person familiar (via Reuters at 4:17p, Yahoo Finance, Grafa); as of this evening the company had not announced the price or filed a final prospectus (Finwire). At the 825 million shares originally marketed that is about **$68.5B**, plus a $26B private placement at the IPO price (Nvidia and Google about $10B each), the largest listing ever; the WSJ put the valuation at about $1.5–1.6 trillion (via Finwire). Orders were reported at nearly seven times the shares on offer (Yahoo Finance). Shares are expected to start trading Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market as **ANT**, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading. Polymarket prices a listing by Nov 19 at 99%.

stories.title: S&P 500 falls a fifth day as health insurers sink; Nasdaq edges up.
stories.body: The S&P 500 slipped 0.23% to 7,323.63 Wednesday, its fifth straight loss and longest losing streak since June (CNBC via StockTitan), and the Dow fell 561.25 points (1.11%) to 50,198.17, while the Nasdaq rose 0.42% to 24,429.88 and the Russell 2000 gained about 0.5% (Vista Partners, Yahoo Finance). Health insurers led the losses after CMS proposed a Medicare Advantage anti-fraud rule that would apply audit findings from sample charts to whole contracts and claw back overpayments back to 2018 (TIKR, Yahoo Finance): UnitedHealth −10.2%, Humana −13%, Elevance −7.6% and Centene −7.1% (StockTitan). The proposal is open for comment until Jan 19, 2027, and Oppenheimer expects legal challenges (via TIKR). Health care (XLV −2.2%) and energy (XLE −3.3%) were the weakest sector ETFs and consumer discretionary (XLY +1.8%) the best. Cybersecurity rallied, with CrowdStrike +8.3% and SentinelOne +10.8% (24/7 Wall St). The VIX eased 3.5% to 24.56 (Cboe), but CNN's Fear & Greed index slipped to 24.6, extreme fear.

stories.title: Nvidia slides 2.9% despite its beat; board shuts the door on Huang.
stories.body: Nvidia closed **−2.9% at $150.96** Wednesday, a fifth straight loss, after being up about 3% before the open on its fiscal Q3 beat: revenue **$115.8B** (+103%, data center $107.6B) vs about $109B expected, non-GAAP EPS **$2.68** vs about $2.47, and a January-quarter guide of **$130B ±3%** (14 weeks, no China data-center sales) vs about $125B (company release, CoinDesk, Yahoo Finance). The board added $150B to the buyback (Newsquawk), and BofA reiterated Buy with a $280 target (Yahoo Finance). Chairman Harvey Jones said on the call the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang, with CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO; the WSJ reported the SEC is looking at whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors (via TheStreet), and Nvidia says it will file its 10-Q in the coming weeks. Polymarket gives about 8% that Huang rejoins by Dec 31 (last trade Tuesday night) and about 20% that a permanent CEO is named by then (last trade Monday), with Arm's Rene Haas the favourite at about 28%.

stories.title: TJX and Target rally on beats; Palo Alto raises its outlook.
stories.body: TJX closed up about **8%** after matching at $1.34 a share on sales of $15.95B vs $15.82B and lifting its full-year comp outlook to +4%, and Target reversed a pre-market drop to close up about **4%** after earning $2.65 vs about $2.07 expected (including a $0.50 tariff refund) on comps of +5.6%, its fastest in five years (StockTitan, Motley Fool, company releases). Lowe's beat at $3.10 adjusted, helped by $0.34 of tariff refunds, but trimmed its margin outlook. After the close, Palo Alto Networks reported fiscal Q1 revenue of **$3.44B** (+39%), next-gen security ARR of $9.73B (+66%) and non-GAAP EPS of **$1.05** vs about $0.99 expected, raised its fiscal 2027 outlook to revenue of $14.52–14.57B and EPS of $4.26–4.30, and said it plans to acquire AI model platform Applied Compute (SEC filing); StockTitan reports the deal at $4.5B in stock. The shares, up 9.9% in the session with the cyber rally, gained about 6.5% in early after-hours trading (StockTitan). Next: Walmart Thursday at 7:00a (about $0.63–0.64 on roughly $187B), then Intuit (Polymarket 95% to beat $2.46), Ross, Keysight and Gap after Thursday's close, and BJ's Friday.

stories.title: Oil drops 3% as stockpiles build despite Gulf attacks.
stories.body: WTI fell 3.2% to settle at **$83.26** and Brent 1.3% to **$91.95** Wednesday, and WTI traded near $82 after the settle (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Yahoo Finance). The EIA said US crude stocks rose 3.4 million barrels last week and gasoline about 5 million barrels, as pump prices fell to their lowest since mid-March. Traders shrugged off fresh attacks in the Gulf, with Kuwait and Bahrain intercepting attacks and more strikes on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz, as a stronger dollar, Fed hike talk and computer-driven selling weighed; the December WTI contract expires Friday. Brent is down about a fifth in November from a six-month high in late October, and the IEA sees a surplus of about 2 million barrels a day this quarter. OPEC+ meets Nov 29 on 2027 policy.
